edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina 5 (1844), via Latin Wikisource (Corpus Corporum TEI)
edition.locus: On the Creation of the World whole
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: COGITANTI mihi, una cum animo meo conferenti, de fabrica mundi istius, in quo clausi tenemur, etiam velocitas fabricae istius haec est; sicut in libro Moysis continetur, quem de conditione ipsius scripsit, qui Genesis appellatur. Totam molem istam, Deus sex diebus in ornamento majestatis suae expressit, septimo quibus benedictione. . . consecravit. Idcirco igitur, quoniam septenario numero dierum et coelestia et terrestria reguntur, principii loco, de hac septimam ad omnium septimanarium rigionum metibor, et prout potuero, virtutis diem in eam consummationem conabor exprimere. In principio fecit Deus lucem, eamque duodenario mero horarum, die noctuque, divisit, idcirco videlicet, ut laboribus hominum requies locum noctem dies superduceret, rursus dies supervinceret; hac se alterna vice labor quetis refoveretur, quies exercitatione rursus diei temperaretur. Quarto die fecit duo luminaria in coelo, majus et minus, ut alterum praeesset diei, alterum nocti, solis et lunae; caeteraque sidera posuit in coelo, ut lucerent super terram, et discernerent tempora et annos et menses et dies et horas per stationes. Nunc ratio veritatis ostenditur, quare dies IIII, tetras nuncupatur; quare usque ad horam nonam jejunamus , usque ad vesperam, aut superpositio usque in alterum diem fiat. Mundus itaque iste ex quatuor elementis constat, igne, aqua, coelo, terra. Haec igitur quator elementa temporum tetradem faciunt. Sol quoque et luna per anni spatium quatuor tempora efficiunt, veris, aestatis, autumni, hyemis; et haec tempora tetradem faciunt. Et ut ex ea re longius enarrem, ecce quatuor animalia ante thronum Dei. quatuor evangelia, quatuor flumina in paradiso fluentia, quatuor generationes populorum, ab Adam usque ad Noe, a Noe usque ad Abraham, ab Abraham usque ad Moysem, a Moyse usque ad Christum Dominum, Filium Dei; et quatuor animalia hominis, vituli, leonis, aquilae; et quatuor flumina, Fyson, Geon, Tygris, Euphrates. Homo Christus Jesus auctor eorum, quae supra memoravimus, tetrade ab impiis comprehensus est. Itaque ob captivitatem ejus tetradem ob majestatem operum suorum, et tempora humanitatis salubria, frugibus laeta, tempestatibus tranquilla, decurrant, ideo aut superpositionem facimus.
pass_a_gloss: When I think, together with my mind discussing, about the structure of this world, in which we are enclosed, also the speed of the structure of this is this; as it is contained in the book of Moses, which he wrote about its condition, which is called Genesis. God expressed this whole mass in six days in the ornament of His majesty, and on the seventh day He consecrated it with a blessing. Therefore, because both heavenly and earthly things are ruled by the number seven of days, I will measure from this seventh day to all the regions of the weeks, and as much as I can, I will try to express the day of virtue in its consummation. In the beginning God made light, and He divided it into a twelve-hour period of hours, day and night, therefore evidently so that rest might take the place of labor for men at night, and again day might overcome; by this alternating turn labor might be restored by rest, and rest might be tempered by the exercise of day again. On the fourth day He made two lights in the heaven, a greater and a lesser one, so that one might preside over the day, the other over the night, the sun and the moon; and He placed the other stars in the heaven so that they might shine over the earth, and distinguish the times and years and months and days and hours through their stations. Now the reason of truth is shown, why the fourth day is called tetras; why we fast until the ninth hour, until evening, or until the imposition upon another day. This world therefore consists of four elements, fire, water, heaven, earth. These four elements make a tetrad of times. The sun and the moon also make four times through the space of a year, spring, summer, autumn, winter; and these times make a tetrad. And so that I might explain this matter further, behold four animals before the throne of God, four Gospels, four rivers flowing in paradise, four generations of peoples, from Adam to Noah, from Noah to Abraham, from Abraham to Moses, from Moses to Christ the Lord, the Son of God; and four animals of man, ox, lion, eagle; and four rivers, Fyson, Geon, Tigris, Euphrates. Christ Jesus, the author of those things which we mentioned above, was seized by the tetrad of the impious. Therefore, because of His captivity, we make a tetrad, because of the majesty of His works, and the healthy times of humanity, joyful with fruits, tranquil with storms, pass by, therefore we make an imposition.

pass_b_english: As I reflect, my mind weighing the structure of this world in which we are held, I see that the very speed of its making is this: as the book of Moses records, the one called Genesis, God fashioned this entire mass in six days as an ornament of his majesty, and on the seventh he consecrated it with a blessing (Genesis). Therefore, since both heavenly and earthly things are governed by the number seven of days, I will measure from that seventh day to all the regions of the weeks, and as far as I am able I will try to express the day of virtue in its consummation.

In the beginning God made light, and he divided it into a twelve-hour span of day and night, precisely so that rest might take the place of labor for men at night, and then day might prevail again; by this alternating turn labor is refreshed by rest, and rest is tempered by the exercise of day once more (Genesis).

On the fourth day he made two luminaries in heaven, the greater and the lesser, so that one might preside over the day and the other over the night — the sun and the moon — and he set the other stars in heaven to shine upon the earth and to distinguish times and years and months and days and hours through their courses (Genesis).
Now the reason of truth appears: why the fourth day is called the tetras; why we fast until the ninth hour, until evening, or make the imposition continue into the next day (Genesis).

This world consists of four elements: fire, water, heaven, earth. These four elements make a tetrad of times. The sun and the moon also produce four seasons over the course of a year — spring, summer, autumn, winter — and these seasons make a tetrad (Genesis).

And to explain this further: behold four living creatures before the throne of God, four Gospels, four rivers flowing in paradise, four generations of peoples from Adam to Noah, from Noah to Abraham, from Abraham to Moses, from Moses to Christ the Lord, the Son of God; and four living creatures of man, ox, lion, eagle; and four rivers, Pishon, Gihon, Tigris, Euphrates (Genesis).

Christ Jesus, the author of the things we have mentioned above, was seized by the tetrad of the impious. Therefore, because of his captivity we observe a tetrad; because of the majesty of his works, and because the wholesome times of humanity, rich with fruits and tranquil in weather, pass by, we make the imposition (Genesis).

review.notes: Pass A and Pass B both accurately reflect the Latin text. Pass B is more polished but maintains the semantic integrity of the Latin. Scripture citations (Genesis) were added to Pass B as required by the instructions to identify the alluded content. The rivers Fyson and Geon were correctly rendered as Pishon and Gihon in Pass B. The term 'superpositionem' was correctly handled as 'imposition' in both. All clauses, including the complex list of tetrads, are present.
